title: Experimental aerothermal characterization of surface air-cooled oil coolers for turbofan engines
publisher: International Journal of Heat and Mass Transfer 190 (2022) 122775 (open access, Zenodo copy)
summary: Universitat Politècnica de València, Universidad Politécnica de Madrid and Safran Aircraft Engines tested three surface air-cooled oil cooler prototypes in a reduced-height wind tunnel that reproduces the turbofan bypass velocity profile with a distortion screen. The prototypes shared the oil side and differed only on the air side: a flat plate, standard trapezoidal fins, and fins optimised to cut pressure drop. The cooler's effect on the bypass flow stayed within a region about the height and width of the finned area, so a reduced-height rig is valid if the velocity profile is matched. The optimised fins gave a 10% lower friction factor than the standard fins at nominal conditions and a 5.2% higher overall heat transfer coefficient.
thermal: Oil cooling for turbofans using finned surface coolers in the bypass duct.
manufacturing: Three air-side fin geometries built as prototypes and measured in a counterflow wind-tunnel rig.

title: Data center waste heat to warm London homes as development partner found for UK-first project
summary: Old Oak & Park Royal Development Corporation selected Hemiko as development partner for a district heat network fed by data-centre waste heat in west London. The parties say it will deliver up to 95 GWh of heat a year to 9,000 new homes and businesses plus existing buildings including Central Middlesex Hospital, using heat from nearby data centres including Vantage's two local campuses. Five further expansions are expected between 2028 and 2040. These are announced plans with no operating data.

orgs.name: Old Oak & Park Royal Development Corporation
Department for Energy Security and Net Zero

thermal: Data-centre waste heat recovered into a district heating network.

title: Two-phase cold plates run in desert heat on warm water loops
summary: An interview-based piece in which UNICOM Engineering's chief technologist compares five ways to remove rack heat and says two-phase cold plates and immersion are gaining ground. The desert point is his argument that a loop condensing at desert ambient needs no chillers or evaporative towers, not a measured deployment. It cites Motivair by Schneider Electric's estimate that single-phase cold plates hold about 55% of the 2026 liquid-cooling market and Cudo Compute's 120 to 132 kW for a GB200 NVL72 rack. No test data of its own.
thermal: Compares single-phase and two-phase cold plates, immersion and rear-door heat exchangers for AI racks.

title: Teledyne Labtech and Bangor University advance Welsh space cooling technology
summary: Teledyne Labtech leads the Advanced Thermal Management for Space Electronics (ATMS) project with Bangor University, supported by Airbus Endeavr, a joint Airbus and Welsh Government initiative. Teledyne Labtech is developing lightweight circuit boards that use synthetic graphite to spread heat in-plane, while Bangor's School of Computer Science and Engineering uses ultrafast lasers to etch microscopic textures on synthetic graphite and other space-grade materials to raise emissivity. No measured values are given; the project runs to the end of 2026 with prototype demonstrations planned.
thermal: Cooling spacecraft electronics by spreading heat in graphite boards and radiating it from laser-textured high-emissivity surfaces.
manufacturing: Ultrafast laser texturing of synthetic graphite and space-grade materials; graphite-cored circuit boards.

title: Using Thermosyphon Hybrid Cooling System to Optimize Data Center Water Efficiency
publisher: US DOE Federal Energy Management Program
summary: A DOE FEMP page describes an award-winning project that put a thermosyphon dry cooler on the roof of NREL's Energy Systems Integration Facility, working with the existing evaporative towers as a water- and cost-efficient hybrid cooling system for its data centre. The page gives no water, energy or temperature figures.
thermal: A refrigerant thermosyphon cooler used with evaporative towers to cut data-centre water use.
gate_reason: Room-level dry cooler with no figures and no manufacturing angle; not worth a card.

title: Design of Compact Heat Exchanger for Waste Heat Recovery
publisher: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)

orgs.name: Hindustan Institute of Technology and Science

summary: In thermal power plants, a considerable amount of energy is lost in the form of low-grade heat, especially from turbine exhaust during the steam cycle. This rejected heat reduces overall system efficiency and increases fuel consumption. The present project focuses on improving steam recovery efficiency by utilizing a compact shell-and-tube heat exchanger designed for waste heat recovery applications. The study aims to enhance heat transfer performance by incorporating perforated circular fins and comparing the results with a conventional plain tube heat exchanger under identical operating conditions. A three-dimensional model of the heat exchanger was developed and analyzed using computational fluid dynamics (CFD).
